title: Termination token precedence bug causing customer evaluation truncation
creator: Maya Patel
description: A high-severity customer escalation reported that their evaluation prompt sets began truncating generations after a serving change that adjusted sampling defaults. The symptom: expected completions were cut short mid-sentence when specific termination markers were present in prompts or instruction templates. The regression affected Hosted and Dedicated customers immediately and Private deployments with the latest agent bundle after upgrade.
incident_summary: Customer A and two enterprise customers opened escalations after daily evals showed a sudden increase in truncated outputs. Investigation found divergence between streaming and non-streaming code paths and an unintended change in runtime precedence: the runtime allowed sampling heuristics (top-p/top-k with early-stopping heuristics) to preempt explicit termination markers in some conditions. This caused models to stop token emission earlier than the configured termination tokens would indicate for prompts containing embedded terminators or dynamic prompt suffixes.
root_cause: During the sampling-default consolidation (runtime-1.19), we introduced a refactor to unify early-stop heuristics across kernels. A subtle ordering change made 'sampling-early-stop' run before 'explicit-terminator-check' in the non-streaming decode loop when sequence-length buckets triggered the accelerated kernel. Streaming decode preserved the old ordering, so behavior diverged across deployment modes and model variants. The net effect: for certain prompt shapes and temperature/top-p combinations, sampling heuristics caused premature termination, overriding explicit termination tokens.
reproduction_steps: Load the model vX on the runtime-1.19 binary with default sampling consolidation enabled
Send prompt containing an embedded termination marker (e.g., '### END ###') followed by an instruction to continue until the marker
Use sampling params: temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, max_tokens=200, streaming=false
Observe truncated output that stops before the termination marker in non-streaming path
Repeat same request with streaming=true and observe compliant termination (old behavior)
investigation_notes: Found a small but critical reordering in decode_main.cc where should_check_terminator() was called after apply_sampling_heuristics() for accelerated kernels
KV cache state was unchanged; not a cache corruption issue
Failure reproduced deterministically on CPU/runtime test harness with a 3-token prompt suffix pattern
Affected models: decoder-only family with short-stop-token suffixes; emerged at scale for customers with long eval prompts that append dynamic examples
Logs showed mismatch in 'terminated_by' metadata between stream and non-stream code paths
mitigations_and_hotfixes: Rolled runtime-1.19.1 hotfix that restores explicit-terminator precedence across all decode kernels
Backported hotfix to Dedicated GPU pool images and published a VPC/private agent patch for on-prem customers
Added temporary customer-config knob 'runtime.strict_terminator_precedence' (true by default) to allow immediate fixes without full rollout
Coordinated with Support to push targeted config changes for the three impacted customers within 4 hours
Deployed an internal canary for the hotfix and monitored eval dashboards for 72 hours
resolution: Hotfix deployed to hosted fleet and Dedicated pools; private customers given an agent patch and rollback instructions. Post-deploy metrics show truncation rate returned to baseline for all impacted customers. Customers acknowledged the fix; two signed off on postmortems and asked for additional safeguards.
follow_up_tasks: Add unit tests that assert termination-token precedence across streaming and non-streaming paths and for accelerated kernels (ENG-20736)
Create an end-to-end regression test using representative customer eval sets and run in CI (ENG-20737)
Improve sampling/terminator interaction docs in the runtime design doc and release notes (ENG-20738)
Audit recent kernel refactors for similar ordering-sensitive changes
Add an observability metric 'termination_source' that labels whether termination was due to explicit token, max_tokens, or heuristic
Schedule a postmortem writeup and customer-facing incident summary for legal and account teams
